resources.string: The app recommends. The runner decides. The plan adapts.
No account needed. Your settings stay on this device. There are no ads, subscriptions or analytics.
Fitness guidance, not medical care. If you experience chest pain, fainting, severe difficulty breathing or serious injury symptoms, stop exercise and seek appropriate medical advice.
I have a specific race in mind
A race date will anchor your future training plan.
General fitness does not need a race or finishing-time target.
Choose a race date, or turn off the specific-race option.
How would you like to approach your goal?
Finish: focus on completing the distance comfortably.
Maximum performance: work toward your strongest realistic performance without a fixed finishing-time target.
Enter a target time to calculate average race pace.
Build the endurance foundation for your distance before gradually adding more race-specific speed work.
Develop endurance and speed together, with room for recovery.
A preference for more threshold, interval and race-pace work. Selecting it for the first time requires supporting recent training evidence.
Your current evidence does not support a new Performance selection. Choose another strategy or review your baseline. You can still choose Maximum Performance as your race goal.

Your current evidence does not support extra performance-focused workload. Performance is your saved preference: you can keep it or choose another strategy. Keeping it does not confirm training readiness, and nothing changes until you save.
Lower-intensity training option designed to build aerobic endurance while limiting unnecessary high-intensity workload.
Choose the days that usually work for you. Select at least as many days as your planned runs per week.
Running and gym training can share a day. Gym days do not replace running days.
Fixed keeps your preferred days consistent; flexible leaves room to move sessions around your week.
Check your goals and weekly routine. You can change these later in Settings.
